hints.title: Simultaneous Contamination Spread Obstacle
hints.text: Multiple rotten oranges contaminate adjacent fresh ones simultaneously each minute. How can you model the parallel spread across all contamination fronts to determine the exact minimum time until no fresh oranges remain?

hints.title: Multi-Source Frontier Invariant
hints.text: Tracking contamination level by level from all initial rotten sources simultaneously models the elapsed minutes until either all fresh items spoil or unreachable items remain.

hints.title: Frontier Level Processing Procedure
hints.text: Count all fresh oranges and gather all initially rotten coordinates. If no fresh oranges exist, return 0. Process the frontier level by level; for each rotten position, convert unvisited fresh neighbors to rotten, decrement the fresh count, and add them to the next time step. Return elapsed minutes if fresh reaches 0, otherwise -1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every cell is queued and processed at most once. Auxiliary space is bounded by the grid dimensions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating minute-by-minute with full grid rescans takes O((M*N)^2) time and risks misidentifying newly rotten oranges as old ones in the same round.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A level-by-level frontier queue ensures linear O(M*N) time and strictly captures simultaneous expansion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Multi-source initialization, correctly counting minutes only when fresh oranges rot, edge case where fresh count starts at 0.
